main_text.p: Hæc Picolominæus partim rationi consentanea, partim repugnantia. Quòd enim illius fluxus, refluxusque magis regimen Lunæ tribuat, id rationes prædictæ falsi evincunt, ut clarius ex dicendis elucescet.
main_text.head: ARTICVLVS V. Cur mare fit elatius in medio quàm juxta littus?
main_text.p: CAufæ æstus maris explicatio præmittit alius causæ notitiam, Cur scilicet mare circa medium magis, quàm juxta littus extollatur. Cujus ratio facilis erit, si quæ verissima Picolominæus mox docuit de halitibus, ac spiritibus calidis, quibus mare gravidatur, memoriâ recolamus. Addamus quæ in corpore animali docet Experientia, frigore scilicet hyberno, partes calidiores intrò se recipere, ac sese quasi in centrum cogere, ut propterea hyeme animantia melius concoquant quàm æstate. Id autem in aliis observare facile est, ex quo & terræ motus, & fulguris, & tonitrui, & complurium in aëre inflammationum causa petenda est, ut suo loco explicabitur. Quantum verò præsenti quæstioni satis est, consideremus flumina undique aquam frigidam in mare advehere, quæ aqua circa littus[?] potissimùm sese diffundat. Hinc Spiritus illi atque halitus, partesque calidæ sese subducentes, haud secus atque hyemali rigore calidæ animalis partes imum petunt, undique in medium mare se contrahant: ubi propter congregationem vim nactæ majorem rarefactione sui mare inflent: quod tamen ibi consistat, facilè ad littus sese diffundat, ob amicitiam partium, quæ ut magis uniantur appetunt figuram globosam. Unde fit, ut in scypho, vel alio vase aqua superemineat, antequam

page.notes: The large initial C of the first word of the paragraph is joined to the word as "CAufæ"; the word is probably "Causæ" with the initial enlarged. "littus" in the paragraph near the middle is read with some doubt. Long s is written as plain s throughout (the printed ligature "ff" in "veriffima" and "fcilicet" is transcribed as "verissima" and "scilicet"). The word "quam" at the foot right is the catchword, and the paragraph continues on the next page. Small dark marks along the margins are stains and show-through, not printed text.
